{{recipesummary|category=Salad recipes|servings=2|time=5 minutes|difficulty=1|image=[[Image:Nest of Carrot Salad, by LadyofProcrastination.jpg|300px]]}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian cuisine]]

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrots]] (about 4 medium sized)
*[[Cookbook:Almond Oil|Almond oil]]
*White balsalmic [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] (or a mix of two parts red wine vinegar to one part balsamic vinegar)
*Coarse [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
*[[Cookbook:Pine Nut|Pine nuts]]

*Fresh greens like matzumi or baby Chinese [[Cookbook:Mustard Greens|mustard]], or even Boston [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Chives|Chives]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Julienne|Julliene]] the carrots (or [[Cookbook:Grating|grate]] them if julienning is not feasible).
# Coat with about 1–2 tablespoons of almond oil.
# Sprinkle generously with vinegar, salt, and pepper.
# Add a hefty serving of pine nuts.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Carrot salad wrapped in greens: Place a little bit of the carrot salad on a green leaf and wrap it up, tying it with a chive. They make about 2-bite hors d'œuvres that are light, healthy, and surprisingly filling. If you can get a-hold of the young mustard greens, they add a fantastic spiciness to it that can't be matched.
